newsitem.title: GERMANY: Anti-Nazi protesters block road to German cemetery.
newsitem.headline: Anti-Nazi protesters block road to German cemetery.

text.p: Protesters blocked the entrance to an east German cemetery where war veterans decorated with a top Nazi-era medal were due to hold a memorial ceremony, police said on Sunday.

Around 100 demonstrators, mostly young people carrying placards with slogans such as "Are Priebke, Karadzic and Mladic taking part too?", sat down in the road leading to the cemetery before the Saturday memorial service was due to begin.
The Knights of the Iron Cross said they were abandoning all public events scheduled for their weekend reunion in Dresden in face of repeated protests.

The Knight's Cross was introduced by the Nazis as a World War Two decoration. Critics say those awarded the medal include participants in the brutal suppression of the 1943 Warsaw ghetto uprising and other atrocities.
"We see the decision by the Knights of the Iron Cross to cancel all public events as a success for our protests against this shameful event," demonstrators said in a statement.
Police said they broke up the protest after the activists began to hit and insult passers-by. They detained 45 protesters but released them after brief questioning.
